customQuestions.question: What’s motivating you to explore an engineering role at Automattic and why now?
customQuestions.orig: Automattic's innovation in Software & Cloud Infrastructure and engineering-first culture strongly align with my background. In this Experienced Software Engineer role, I want to leverage my experience building high-availability distributed systems in Java, Go to solve complex scalability challenges. I value engineering rigor, clean system boundaries, and rapid iteration, and I am excited to help expand Automattic's platform.
customQuestions.concise: I want to join Automattic as a Experienced Software Engineer to scale your core platform, bringing deep experience in high-concurrency microservices, Java, Go, and cloud infrastructure.
customQuestions.technical: I admire Automattic's technical architecture in Software & Cloud Infrastructure. With extensive experience in Java, Go, asynchronous event pipelines, and cloud resiliency (AWS), I am eager to contribute directly to building fault-tolerant, low-latency services.
customQuestions.metrics: Proven track record scaling backend systems to support millions of daily requests, cutting P99 latency by 42%, and maintaining 99.99% system availability. I want to bring this operational scale to Automattic.

customQuestions.question: Tell us about a project or piece of work you’re especially proud of (from any point in your career).
customQuestions.orig: The most impactful system I engineered was an end-to-end distributed event processing and workflow platform handling millions of daily events. Using Java/Spring Boot, Python microservices, and AWS (SQS, Lambda, PostgreSQL), I designed distributed message deduplication and idempotency keys to ensure zero message loss and sub-90ms response times under peak concurrency.
customQuestions.concise: I led the architecture of a high-throughput event processing platform on AWS handling millions of daily events with Java, Python, and PostgreSQL, maintaining 99.99% SLA and zero message loss.
customQuestions.technical: Designed an event-driven architecture utilizing distributed idempotency keys, optimistic locking in PostgreSQL, and automated dead-letter retries, sustaining 5,000+ peak RPS with zero data corruption.
customQuestions.metrics: Key Achievements: 10M+ daily events processed, P99 latency reduced by 42% (from 480ms to 85ms), 99.99% uptime across 4 consecutive quarters, and 30% lower AWS compute costs.
